nodes.summary: There is a finitely generated group $G$ such that the quasivariety $qG$ generated by $G$ has infinitely many maximal proper subquasivarieties: for every natural number $k$ there are sets of quasi-identities $Q_0, \dots, Q_{k-1}$, each defining a maximal proper subquasivariety of $qG$, such that for $i \ne j$ the quasivarieties defined by $Q_i$ and $Q_j$ are different.
nodes.title: Some finitely generated group has infinitely many maximal subquasivarieties

nodes.summary: The statement that there is a finitely generated group $G$ such that the quasivariety $qG$ generated by $G$ has infinitely many maximal proper subquasivarieties: for every natural number $k$ there are sets of quasi-identities $Q_0, \dots, Q_{k-1}$, each defining a maximal proper subquasivariety of $qG$, such that for $i \ne j$ the quasivarieties defined by $Q_i$ and $Q_j$ are different.
nodes.title: Budkin's problem on maximal subquasivarieties (Kourovka 14.25)

nodes.summary: A quasi-identity $\forall x\,(w_1 = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge w_k = 1 \to w = 1)$ in the unknowns $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ holds in a group $G$ when every assignment of elements of $G$ to the unknowns under which each premise $w_1, \dots, w_k$ evaluates to $1$ in $G$ also makes the conclusion $w$ evaluate to $1$.
nodes.title: Quasi-identities holding in a group

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and let $qG$ be the quasivariety generated by $G$, that is, the quasivariety defined by the set of all quasi-identities that hold in $G$. A set $Q$ of quasi-identities defines a maximal proper subquasivariety of $qG$ when the quasivariety defined by $Q$ is contained in $qG$ but does not contain $qG$, and every quasivariety $V$ defined by a set of quasi-identities with $V$ containing the…
nodes.title: Maximal proper subquasivarieties

nodes.summary: For a set $Q$ of quasi-identities, a group $H$ belongs to the quasivariety defined by $Q$ when every quasi-identity in $Q$ holds in $H$. Every quasivariety of groups has this form.
nodes.title: The quasivariety defined by a set of quasi-identities

nodes.summary: A quasi-identity in $n$ unknowns $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ is a formula $\forall x\,(w_1 = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge w_k = 1 \to w = 1)$, given by the number $n$, a finite list of premises $w_1, \dots, w_k$ and a conclusion $w$, all of them elements of the free group on $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$.
nodes.title: Quasi-identities of groups

nodes.summary: The quasi-theory of a group $G$ is the set of all quasi-identities that hold in $G$. The quasivariety defined by this set is the quasivariety $qG$ generated by $G$.
nodes.title: The quasi-identities of a group

nodes.summary: For sets $Q_1$ and $Q_2$ of quasi-identities, the quasivariety defined by $Q_1$ is contained in the quasivariety defined by $Q_2$: every group in which all quasi-identities of $Q_1$ hold also satisfies all quasi-identities of $Q_2$.
nodes.title: Inclusion of quasivarieties

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
